title: Eleven Letters and One Visit
subtitle: 亲属与家庭 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 亲属与家庭（生活与学习·家庭与亲情）
meta: 主题语境：亲属与家庭（生活与学习·家庭与亲情）　|　核心词汇：cousin　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 cousin 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1959 my mother ① wrote to a cousin she had last seen eleven summers before, and she said the writing was the whole of the visiting. The ② cousin, meaning the person and not the letter, answered in four lines and stayed that brief; cousin, she said, is the only thing in a family that is judged by how little it needs explaining.

Every ③ cousin in that photograph had the same chin, and the ④ cousin at the end, meaning the one nobody could place and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever pointed out twice. Cousin, my grandmother said, is nine parts chin and one part somebody willing to place them; my mother said the placing is the part that fills the photograph.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ cousin was the whole of the argument, meaning the distant relation and not the person. The ⑥ cousin, meaning the distant relation and not any of that, is the only thing in an argument that everybody claims and nobody counts; cousin, he said, is either someone you write to or the only word that means both a person and a distant relation. She said the distant relation is the part they remember.

By 1967 the ⑦ cousin had become a line in a family tree, and the tree had become an argument about the chin. The ⑧ cousin of the whole thing, my mother wrote in August, was one letter and thirty years of placing; cousin, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to write. He said the writing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ cousin I remember is the one at the end, who answered in 1973 and is still described as the briefest in the county. A ⑩ cousin, my grandmother said in 1975, is the only thing that improves by being placed; every cousin, she said, is a distant relation that has agreed to look like a person. She said the distant relation was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 堂（表）兄弟；堂（表）姐妹
B. n. 表亲（指那个人本身，与那封信相对）
C. 固定搭配：write to a cousin 给表亲写信
D. n. 表亲（指那张照片里每一位）
E. n. 表亲（指末尾那一位）
F. n. 远亲；同族（抽象：血缘较远的亲戚）
G. n. 表亲（指家谱里提到的那一位）
H. n. 同辈亲属（抽象总称）

items.q: wrote to a cousin she had last seen eleven summers before
The cousin, meaning the person and not the letter
cousin was the whole of the argument
The cousin, meaning the distant relation

The cousin of the whole thing

answers.why: write to a cousin 意为“给表亲写信”，1959 年母亲给一位她十一个夏天前见过的表亲写了信。
cousin 意为“表亲”，指那个人本身而不是那封信，回信只有四行。
cousin 指那张照片里每一位表亲，每一位都是同样的下巴。
cousin 指末尾那一位（没人认得出是哪一房的那一房），是唯一有人指出过两次的。
cousin 意为“远亲、同族”，父亲说远亲就是那场争论的全部，指的是血缘较远的亲戚而不是那个人。
cousin 为抽象用法，指血缘较远的亲戚关系而不是那个人，是争论里人人都攀、却无人计算的东西。
cousin 意为“表亲”，指家谱里提到的那一位，到 1967 年这位表亲成了家谱里的一行。
cousin 意为“同辈亲属”，母亲八月写道，整件事的同辈亲属是一封信三十年的辨认。
cousin 意为“堂（表）兄弟、姐妹”，我记得的是末尾那一位，1973 年回信，至今仍被说成全县写得最短的。
cousin 为抽象总称，祖母说一位表亲是唯一会因为被认出而变好的东西。
